title: JR East Introducing 'Hands-Free' Shinkansen Bag Drop
paragraphs: Carrying a large suitcase on a crowded train can be difficult. Now, a Japanese railway company is making it easier for travelers to send their bags by bullet train.

JR East, a large railway company in eastern Japan, has a program called "JRE Hands-Free Travel." On August 1, 2026, it started a new service that lets travelers leave their bags in special lockers at Tokyo Station and Sendai Station. The bags are then sent on the Shinkansen to a hotel in the other city on the same day.

The service is quite easy to use. First, travelers book a locker on the Multi-Ecube website. Reservations must be made by 9:30 a.m. on the day of travel. Then, travelers put their bags in the locker by 10:30 a.m. JR East carries the bags on the Shinkansen using its Hakobyun Quick delivery service, and the bags arrive at the traveler's hotel later that day. Each locker holds one bag, and the price depends on the size of the locker. It costs 3,500 yen for a small locker, 3,600 yen for a medium locker and 3,700 yen for a large locker.

Before, travelers could only use lockers to send bags to hotels nearby. This is the first time that bags can be sent to another prefecture on the same day using lockers. Tokyo and Sendai are about 350 kilometers apart. The trip takes about one and a half hours by Shinkansen, but about three and a half hours by road.
JR East plans to expand the service further in the future. From autumn 2026, travelers will be able to leave their bags in lockers in Tokyo and send them to counters at Narita and Haneda airports.
The service may also help make trains and stations less crowded, because fewer people will carry large suitcases on board.
